Subject: Quick Q — breakpoint refund waterfall for multi-year prepay

Neha —

Thanks for the term sheet. Two quick clarifying items from procurement before we route to legal:

1) Breakpoint behavior: if Helix hits only 40% of Year 2 estimated usage and wants to step down to a lower tier, how does Redwood calculate the refund or credit? Is it an immediate cash refund, a credit applied to future invoices, or an amortized approach?

2) Early termination carve-outs: there's a proposed 180-day no-refund guardrail for early term — can you confirm whether that is absolute or if material breach / prolonged downtime exceptions apply?

We're trying to align this with our existing vendor calendar (co-terming with a Feb 1 renewal). If we move forward, procurement would like an explicit co-term clause and an example waterfall for a 3-year, annual-prepay model with ramp breakpoints.

Appreciate a quick sketch so we can decide next steps.

Best,

Helix.ai

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Quick Q — breakpoint refund waterfall for multi-year prepay

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the clear asks. Summary answers below; attaching a worked example and the latest term sheet (v3) for redlines.

1) Breakpoint / stepdown refund mechanics (short):
- Tiered refund credit: by default we apply a pro-rata credit back to the customer on the unused prepaid portion when the customer elects to step down. Credits are calculated on a per-year basis and applied to future usage or refunded at customer request.
- Amortized protection: for multi-year discounts tied to committed prepay we apply an amortization schedule so the effective refund equals prepaid minus recognized consumption and amortized discount; this avoids full refund of upfront discounts.
- Example: in the attached "helix_proposed_ramp_schedule.csv" we show Year 2 at 60% usage; the customer receives a credit equal to unused token value less the annualized discount amortization.

2) Early termination carve-outs:
- The 180-day no-refund clause is intended as a deterrent to churn post-commit; it is not absolute. We always preserve refunds for: material breach (defined), prolonged outage exceeding SLA credit thresholds, and regulatory orders.
- We can propose explicit language that enumerates exceptions (material breach, <90% availability for N consecutive weeks, or force majeure).

3) Co-terming & alignment:
- We can add co-term language to align the Redwood contract to Feb 1 renewal; two options: (A) co-term by pro-rating remaining prepaid value into a short alignment tranche, or (B) allow a one-time co-term payout/credit to match your vendor date. Option (A) is lower operational overhead for us, option (B) is more flexible for Helix.

Next steps: I propose we (a) confirm which co-term option Helix prefers, (b) I circulate redline language for the refund waterfall, and (c) we schedule a 30-min procurement walk-through.

I've attached redwood_term_sheet_v3.xlsx and helix_proposed_ramp_schedule.csv with the numeric waterfall.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor

Subject: Fwd: Quick Q — breakpoint refund waterfall for multi-year prepay

Team — looping you both for sign-off / alternative language. See Helix asks below. Key decision points:

- Refund model: default = credit or cash refund; propose amortized discount retention (12-month straight-line amortization on the discount).
- 180-day no-refund: we keep as-is but enumerate exceptions (material breach, SLA outage > X days, regulatory).
- Co-term: recommend Option (A) — pro-rate into a short alignment tranche (less legal friction).

Proposed contract language snippets for legal to consider:
"Upon early termination by Customer, Redwood will refund the unused prepaid balance less the amortized portion of any upfront discount. The upfront discount shall be amortized on a straight-line basis over the applicable 12-month period commencing on the Effective Date of the prepayment. Refunds are subject to exceptions for (i) material breach by Redwood, (ii) sustained SLA failure as defined in Section X, and (iii) regulatory compulsion."

Please reply with edits — Marissa, Rishi, any finance/legal flags?

Thanks,
Neha

Neha —

Appreciate the clarity and the worked example. Procurement preference is Option (B) for co-terming — one-time alignment credit — because our internal billing cycle is rigid and the administrative lift to split a short tranche is non-trivial.

On the 180-day clause: we cannot accept absolute barring of refunds. Can Redwood confirm redlining the clause to explicitly state refunds remain available for material breach and SLA outages (define SLA as 99.5% rolling monthly availability with the agreed credit thresholds)? Also asking to remove the 12-month amortization floor for the customer if Redwood is at fault (e.g., downtime caused by Redwood or critical security failure).

If you can incorporate those two redlines and share an updated term sheet and a simple calculation example showing Option (B) co-term credit application, we can route to legal next week.
